items.title: After E340 the css keystroke and the parse break still pay `check_view_escape`'s one-sweep retaining fixpoint (~50 ms at load) because a LIVE module hands on a view-capturing closure: a summary computed only for the callee asked would remove it, and that needs a body-expression index
items.discussion: lane incr-56 (post-Order 55) on the N186 exhibit (kolt@2684c70): door 2 made the fixpoint one sweep + a worklist over (callee, position) edges and door 1 made it lazy (only a live call handing a view-capturing closure to an ordinary callee asks); the leaf keystroke asks never (retaining-fixpoints=0), css and parse break ask once (~50 ms at load ~30; ~35 ms quiet est.)
items.body: The sweep still walks every expression of the program once to find the retaining positions of every callee; the live call needs only ITS callee's summary. A per-callee summary needs an index from a callee to the body expressions that mention it (a row family in the S7 form, filed per module and served on a hit). Rec: build the index as class D rows beside move_tables.rs's, then compute the summary per asked callee; pin with the census counter `retaining-fixpoints` and the differential. Sizing M.

items.title: `check_view_escape`'s capture scan walks all ~5,900 closures of the program (std's included) on every keystroke that asks, ~16-20 ms: a lazy per-closure memo of 'captures a view' is exact and would make it a lookup
items.discussion: lane incr-56 (post-Order 55): the split of the pass on the base at load ~30 - fixpoint ~430 ms (E340's doors took it), closure scan ~20, sanctioned wrapped calls ~9, the walk ~18
items.body: Whether a closure captures a view is a function of the closure's own body and its captured bindings' types, so a memo keyed by the closure's entity (filed on the record, invalidated with the item) answers the same bits. Rec: the memo in the S7 record form; pin that a served keystroke scans only the hot set's closures (a counter) and the differential. Sizing S.

items.title: One base `parse repair` sample on the N186 exhibit read 50.2 G instructions / 18 s - three times the row's median (17.4 G) - an EXTRA analysis that does not always happen; the harness should name what ran
items.kind: editor latency (measurement; a sporadic extra analysis)
items.discussion: lane incr-56 (post-Order 55), lsp-latency.py --runs 5 on kolt@2684c70 with the base 8e8c463c binary at load 10-50: one of five repair samples at 50.2 G where the others sat at 17.4 G; the lane dropped the cold first run and took the median, so the series' figures are unaffected, but the sample is a real event
items.body: Something ran a whole analysis twice (a second didChange landing before the first settled? a document version race? the std prefix rebuilt?). Rec: have the harness record the phase line (`VILAN_PHASE_TIMING`) and the analysis count per sample so an outlier names its cause; then fix the cause if it is the server's. Sizing S (the recording) + the fix.
